verdict.tagline: A rugged frontier trek with a serious appetite for hardware.
for_you_if: you want a sprawling western grind to sink hours into
you enjoy pushing past early repetition
not_for_you_if: you rely heavily on a controller for aiming
your hardware struggles with high heat and GPU usage

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players struggle with controller aiming, keybind limitations, and interface hurdles.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that changing keybinds is only supported for mouse and keyboard, while controller support has limitations and integration issues.

citations.review_text: I stumbled on this game while doom-scrolling on Steam's store page and had my eye caught by this game. While I haven't even began making a dent in the existing content of this game, the little I've played so far has been incredibly fun and entertaining. This game feels like the result of combining the best aspects of Doom Eternal's combat and enemy logic and Helldivers Two's mission maps and side-objective incentivisation, all while then adding a unique spin to give a whole new flavour of gameplay. The only thing I have of note that could be called a complaint is changing in-game keybinds can only be done for mouse and keyboard, as controller is only semi-compatible during my making of this review. Even so, this is yet to hinder my gameplay in any way besides lack of control optimisation for when I want to do max difficulty missions. From what I've found, Far Far West is an absolute hidden gem with amazing potential once it gets past its early development stage. And I wish the developers the absolute best as they continue to create more content for me and other players to sink our teeth into and enjoy!

Controller support [b]SUCKS[/b]

If your aim ([i]pardon the pun[/i]) is to play with controller, hold off until they "fix" it.

Good luck trying to pick up an item off the floor.
Good luck trying to interact with something.
Why is "ping" on click left stick instead of sprint?
Aiming is a horrendous.

No game is fun, if you have to battle with control method before shooting bad guys.

[i]Proper controller support was requested in April 2026. 
With a developer responding it will be looked into.[/i]

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players notice heavy GPU heat, repetitive map layouts, and a slow grind through unlocks.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game causes hardware to heat up significantly and runs with high GPU usage.

citations.review_text: Actually a fairly good game overall, but it heats my PC way, way more than it ought to. Probably not a good sign, pls work on that.

It's fun, plays to the strengths of the theme very well and it obviously has a very passionate team behind it. The gunplay is fun and I really like the stylization of not only the environment but also of the visual effects. I really like the spell combination system.

While you certainly can play it solo, playing with friends here turns into more of a requirement as you get into the harder difficulties. Yea, you can solo but honestly why would you do that to yourself

I do like this game. It more than likely will be very good and a very strong recommend from me maybe in a year or two from now.

Put concisely the content that is currently present gets stale pretty quickly. Progression through all means (leveling up, unlocking weapons, leveling weapons, unlocking jokers and spells) in this game is slow and very grindy. The missions and zones both become very repetitive very quickly. I do really like the effort put into the side missions / quests but there needs to be more variation. 

Both the progression being very slow and the missions being repetitive make the game feel like it does not respect your time much at the moment.

If you're on the fence I'd maybe wait. Keep an eye on it and wait for it to be refined a bit more.


Smaller gripes:
-This game currently uses so much GPU. It stays at a very stable frame rate but man does my PC heat up fast while playing this game

-The monster house boss just isn't fun IMO. I have no problem aiming at the glowing hit-me spots but really it just takes a long time to down it. Most of the bosses after the first go around feel like they drag on and are bullet spongey.

-The shotgun does not feel like a shotgun, it feels exactly like your starting repeater rifle.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the gameplay loop becomes repetitive quickly due to recycled layouts and a lack of mission variety.

citations.review_text: Well made and enjoyable game, but becomes extremely repetitive very quickly. Hopefully this will improved with future updates.

[h2]What... Don't You Guys Have Friends...?[/h2]
No actually. I don't have a close group of people I can call friends, who are available to mess around with and have fun in co-op shooters or adventures. Far Far West does not deserve its overwhelmingly positive ratings, if you’re someone who prefers to play solo. If you don’t already have a close group of friends to mess around with in co-op shooters or adventures, this game quickly loses its appeal, because there is nothing outside of the fast paced vibes.

Visually, it tries to blend Sea of Thieves and The Wild Wild West, and it layers on fast-paced music, honestly, the soundtrack is the only thing that gives the game life. Every stage across every quadrant is just a recycled layout with minor event tweaks that end up feeling identical. The repetition is exhausting: you’re forced to grind mission after mission for new weapon blueprints, needing five or six runs just to unlock one, and each one comes with their own built in leveling system, which is even more of a grind, and when you finally hit level 100 and prestige, the so-called rewards are mere stat tweaks or underwhelming bonuses, like adding a few more "chance to drop joker cards", not exactly game-changing.

Playing solo is mindlessly boring, and the thrill evaporates fast when playing with triple pristiged golliaths that one tap everything on Very Hard or Nightmare mode, where you can't exactly do a whole lot on your own. They mention a roadmap for future content, but with a foundation this bland and uninspired outside of friends and gunslinging, I doubt any update will fix the core issues. Without the music, there’s nothing here to keep you coming back. It’s briefly fun, but the novelty wears off almost immediately.

Not a contrarian. I am just blunt and realistic. The music is a banger, it keeps you here.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the map layouts as repetitive since missions reuse the same maps with only side objectives and bosses changing.

citations.review_text:
We didnt get rayman 4, but this comes very very close to it.

Gameplay is mostly similar to helldiver 2 EXCEPT the maps will always be the same and only the side objective and boss changes.

This game is all the good parts of games like RoR2 and has an awesome cartoony artstyle similar to DRG and TF2. It is always instant fun within a minute and so far it feels like there is always something to grind towards, drawing you in again and again. Also, the music is genuinely amazing and makes you feel really REALLY cool. The weapons are well made, the spells are fun, jokers are pretty easy to understand, and the in game resources are pretty fun to get. every  mission feels well made and a lot of the pseudo-missions are pretty fun.

9.5/10 (could use more variety in missions instead of objective, boss, escape; first hour or two is prettys slow, but it really gets started once you have proper weapons, spells, and a barebones build)

There is SO much more I could talk about for how cool this game is, but that would take ages. PLAY THIS GAME.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that progression through unlocks and leveling is slow and grindy.

citations.review_text:
Not Recommended

Far Far West has some potential, but in its current state it feels way too barebones for a roguelite.

My biggest issue is the lack of meaningful progression. One of the main things I enjoy about roguelites is that even when a run ends, you still feel like you're working towards something — unlocking new upgrades, abilities, characters, weapons, or other permanent progression that makes future runs more interesting. Far Far West doesn't really give me that feeling. The runs start to feel repetitive instead of feeling like I'm gradually building towards something.

The bosses are also pretty boring and don't feel particularly memorable or exciting to fight. The quest lines are extremely simple and quickly become repetitive, so there isn't much there to keep me invested either.

On top of that, there's a lack of achievements, which removes another reason to keep playing or work towards specific challenges.

I don't think Far Far West is necessarily a bad concept. There is definitely some potential here, and with more content it could become a much better roguelite. It just needs more progression, more interesting bosses, better/more varied quests, more achievements, and generally more things to unlock and work towards between runs.

For now, though, there simply isn't enough here for me to recommend it.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Longer sessions reveal initial stutter, punishing solo death loops, and deep individual weapon and magic progression grinds.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe stuttering and lag during initial shader compilation upon starting the game.

citations.review_text: its a good twist on the hoard shooter view, but its still beta so my frames will be fine and then just start sucking and i have to reset the game every little wile, and it wont stop unless i do that. but that's the only problem

The only one single gripe is the starting up. If you need to compile all the shaders, just pause everything and let the shaders cook. Its fine, we go through gacha games that do this and we are willing. Its worse to play thru the tutorial with stutters and laggy responses rather than just waiting 10 minutes. I nearly refunded the game just because of this.

But if you overcome this part, be ready to play helldivers meet Call of Juarez gunslinger meet Hexen. The gameplay is fast paced, horde battles dont lag much, the levelling system is a little grindy but the mission runs aren't boring to the point it feels like a milk run.

The difficulty curve isn't too bad either, and what's more exciting is that this game is still young. For a $15 price tag I would consider this a steal already considering more content and updates are coming. Its helldivers without all the negative stigma that they have built up. Now to find a mod for Megumin voice whenever a nuke goes off.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that progression requires grinding separate levels for individual weapons, magic spell schools, and the hero character.

citations.review_text:
as usual i wish there was a neutral review, but in a sea of positive reviews i want to at least have a chance of my critical one being seen. i know the game is early access but if i am allowed to pay for it on steam i feel as though i can review it under those same conditions. 

at its core Far Far West feels still like a demo of its potential, and i do not think it stands shoulder to shoulder with its predecessors such as Deep Rock. if it was just because the game was limited for content, i would understand, but while that is an issue its not why i write this review.

i think both systems and gameplay have balance issues that i do not understand the persistence of, and while they are subject to change, they have apparently existed through playtests before the launch of the game. i want to break down some of my major gripes after having played through many missions in all difficulties (yes, that includes nightmare) and having played other similar games.

1. Progression 
progression in this game feels strained. as with many games releasing in early access, it feels like its trying to entice the player to view the game as beefy through a lengthy need to grind. i dont necessarily mind a grind, but the way the grind is implemented in this game just feels unneccesary and drawn out. you have to level your magic spell schools, weapons, and hero all individually. to level 100 and back again after a prestige, which is very much not just for fun but for incredibly practical benefit. and you only get levels for your spell schools or weapons when using said tool. sounds "correct" on paper, yet in practice it just makes every mission feel like a chore. desperately trying to make your pathetic dinky boomerang dish out damage and ignoring your fun to use spells just because you want to get some levels, it is not fun whatsoever and leads to playing the game in the way it asks you to, and not in the way you want to. passively grind the weapon you say? good luck. so many weapons will…

Great shooting, incredibly fun movement. Progress on your character, guns, and spells. Tons of unlockables, spell combos, and side quests to find. 12/10 would recommend. 

The devs put in a ton of effort and you can tell from the chill zone and all the mini games. I'm just listing everything it has, its great.

Bought it for wife and I. We've put 30+ hours into it!

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that singleplayer death results in an instant loss without balancing adjustments for playing solo.

citations.review_text:
I will start with saying I am extremely picky about what games I get into. 

After looking at all of the 'helpful' and 'non-helpful' reviews for a couple of days, my wife decided to gift this game to me; leaving the debate of whether, or not, to purchase it out of my hands.

I am very grateful she did! I have already enjoyed countless hours swapping around builds and grinding out the best mechanics for kiting and movement. On top of this, almost every round you play is different based on what types of random joker cards you get. It is very grindy - as in, since it's apparently got more content coming, the content does get more stale around 40 hours of play - BUT If you enjoy movement-based shooters with different styles you have to rebuild from scratch, this game is for you.

This game is obviously more fun and interesting with your friends (if you have any) but is also extremely fun, and almost a little too challenging, solo. It's much easier to kite solo, but much less forgiving; as every movement matters. I did fail quite a few times on nightmare solo. I recently beat a few nightmare rounds! (duo'd, not solo) and I'll quote my buddy (who has about 10-15 hrs in the game) saying, "this [nightmare mode] is like the perfect level of challenging" after we died a couple times. 

I'll end by saying the negativity in the comments/community is extremely disappointing. It's as if folks don't understand how much goes into creating a game. The content creation, the animations, the projectiles, and, hell, even the languages. They expect content to be shoveled at them like fortnite skins.. it's sickening.

If the devs care about their game at all they will take months to a year to come out with any new content we can grind out for hours - we just take that for granted. Especially if the dev team is only 8 people as they claim.. 

(speaking from experience) I challenge any of those negative people to go try to make a game where people shoot at least 2 different guns and tell me…

Fast paced gunplay, yet without time pressure, you can really take your time to explore the levels and engage enemies at your leisure.
Also has a lot of character and style, with how the artstyle and music flows wonderfully everywhere in the game. I do feel like the storm theme and the extraction themes are a bit too similar in my taste, but that's nitpicky.

It is best with friends though. Death in singleplayer is an insta loss and the balancing doesn't feel like it takes this into account.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that enemy AI paths in straight lines towards players, causing enemies to bunch up in single file.

citations.review_text:
Very repetitive gameplay. It can be fun for a few hours, but after that it gets really boring. There's basically no enemy AI since they just walk towards one player in a straight line. They all conga towards you while ignoring everyone else. If something spawned targeting someone who isn't you, you can literally swim inside of them. They will never attack you. Frequently they get caught on invisible walls and they just hold still without even trying to attack you, and sometimes they even get caught on nothing and they just hold still for no reason. Even ranged enemies will stop attacking you when this happens.

Most enemies are also just guys that walk towards you then swing at you. There's one enemy that shoots a slow bullet at you, and one that will hit you with a hitscan beam if you don't shoot him before he finishes charging. That's basically all of the enemies. 

Very little customization is available. There's only a few guns, and most of them feel very similar. The primary weapons are a machinegun, a machinegun that's less accurate, a machinegun that requires you to constantly be holding right click 24/7 because there's no reason not to, a slow sniper, and a less slow sniper. Most of the perks you can put on the weapons don't change how the weapon plays or feels and mostly just increases its damage.

The multiplayer also has people very frequently teamkilling everyone for no reason, so you're probably going to have to play with friends if you don't want to do singleplayer. It's very rare for me to join a game and not see someone start killing everyone and insulting them.

I’ve been sinking a lot of hours into this lately and I'm honestly loving it, the gameplay loop is smooth, the style is unique, and the soundtrack is incredibly solid. I have high hopes for the next updates, but looking at it critically, the reward economy and balancing are currently holding it back. The biggest issue is that the progression feels totally out of whack. The extra XP bonus for difficult terrain is a joke and doesn't justify the extra time spent on the map. Worse, main objectives can vary wildly in duration and difficulty, yet they give zero extra experience. The risk and effort just don't match the reward, and the same goes for the bosses, except for the Saloon, they all melt way too fast. On top of that, the spell balance is completely warped by the enemy AI. They constantly line up in single file, making linear spells like the basic shock vastly superior to options like the basic fire spell for clearing out hordes. Don't get me wrong, the chaotic friendly fire adds a fun, tense layer to the matches, but the overall progression loop needs serious work. It’s still an amazing indie title that's worth every penny, but the devs have some serious balancing to do in the next patches.
